findings: Affix has phonological, spelling, stress and frequency properties but no lexical input/output category contract.
MorphologyConfig has separate prefix and suffix pools and template weights, with no stem category inventory or category transition policy.
planMorphology chooses the template first, then independently samples prefix and suffix by frequency, before root generation.
With both template, positive-frequency prefix/suffix pairs are structurally selectable regardless of their lexical category requirements.
Baseline does not annotate generated roots with observed lexical categories; assigning categories is an explicit model assumption, not evidence extracted from spelling.
Proposed treatment must represent lexical category and input/output transitions as typed structured data; affix homographs may need distinct senses rather than one broad class.
Candidate must preserve licensed paths and weighted opportunities, not simply remove difficult suffixes. Empty compatible pools must have an explicit policy.
Runtime attribution requires disabled-policy output/RNG parity and enabled-policy trace evidence for stem category, transition sequence, eligibility pool and final category.
Q11b control is frozen for queued baseline capture; this audit does not change that checkout or declare it the final Q18 baseline.
measurementRequirements: Exhaustive configured transition/path compatibility including both template and affix senses
Deterministic public-API seeded traces and RNG probes with policy omitted
Registered large-sample category/template/affix opportunities and all permitted-path coverage
Publish independent PR with explicit productivity assumptions; no human-quality claim without observations
